newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel provident funds' results mixed in August.
newsitem.headline: Israel provident funds' results mixed in August.

text.p: Israel's provident funds managed by the top commercial banks had mixed results in August, with most achieving positive yields on a nominal basis but many suffering negative yields on a real basis.
Bank Hapoalim, Israel's leading bank, said all eight of its funds had positive nominal yields ranging from 0.1 to 1.1 percent in August. But on a real basis only two funds posted positive yields.
The bank said it based its calculations on an estimated inflation of 0.3 percent in August.

Bank Leumi, the second largest bank, said 11 of its 14 funds had positive nominal yields ranging from 0.03 to 0.93 percent in August while five had positive real yields ranging from 0.07 to 0.64 percent.
First International Bank of Israel said all six of its funds posted positive nominal yields of 0.24 to 0.49 percent while four also had positive real yields.
In the first eight months, most of the funds at the banks had positive nominal yields but negative real yields.
The provident funds are long-term savings funds with special tax benefits. Weak stock and bond markets have hurt their performance lately, leading to a wave of public redemptions.
In the last week in August the capital market began to turn around, slightly boosting the funds' performances.
